The general arrangement’s words (ferry-ship.js), then the named fittings built in the room (ferry-interior.js).
Design: Emergency-generator room: the 40 kVA emergency generator, the emergency switchboard, the 24 V batteries and their chargers, a 60 L day tank, louvres
Built: emergency generator, emergency switchboard, battery box, day tank
Design: CO₂ room and fire-control station: four 45 kg CO₂ bottles, the release cabinet, the remote fan stops and fuel quick-closing valves, two firemen’s outfits
Built: CO₂ release cabinet, firemen’s outfit locker, fan stops
Design: Crew cabin, two berths: the bosun and the oiler; bunk beds, lockers, a fold-down desk
Design: Johansson’s chief engineer duty cabin
Design: Master’s cabin: a desk, a bunk along the corridor’s wall, the ship’s papers and the safe; the crew stair’s trunk walled off in its outboard forward corner
Design: The crew’s corridor down the middle, from their own door aft onto the bridge deck’s platform (they come up the open deck’s ladders) to the wheelhouse
CREW ACCOMMODATION · the bridge deck house
Emergency generator and CO2 rooms, cabins, crew WC, mess, galley, corridor
Drawn from buildFerryModel() as the game builds it: plans are cut by a horizontal plane and sections by a vertical one, and what is cut
is drawn heavy, what lies beyond in outline. The design (general arrangement, ferry-ship.js) is dashed over each plan: a room built away
Issues are found in her data by tools/ferry-audit.mjs and numbered for the whole set: red a clash, amber a check. Their source lines are

WORKING DRAWINGS OF THE GAME MODEL · Johansson World vessel · no flag, class or construction approval · buildFerryModel() as built, cut and drawn with hidden lines removed · issues from tools/ferry-audit.mjs
